title: Glossary + concept/prerequisite graph for the Python module
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). A machine-readable glossary and concept/prerequisite graph lets the learner site sequence lessons correctly, highlight missing prerequisites, and navigate between concepts. Without it the site is a flat list; with it, learners can find their current level and follow a structured path.
objective: Produce a machine-readable glossary of Python beginner terms and a concept/prerequisite graph linking all lessons in the Python module (batches A, B, C), suitable for use by the learner site's navigation and search features.
acceptanceCriteria: Glossary covers all key terms introduced in the Python module (≈ batches A/B/C); each entry has a term, plain-language definition, and the lesson(s) where it is introduced.
Concept/prerequisite graph is machine-readable (JSON or compatible format) and lists, for each lesson, the concepts it introduces and the concepts/lessons it depends on.
Graph is acyclic (no circular prerequisites); the graph is validated by a CI check.
All glossary and graph data is schema-valid; the dataset is published with a CC-BY-4.0 license declaration.
output: A merged dataset containing the Python module glossary and concept/prerequisite graph in machine-readable format, with provenance and license metadata.
